page.name: Orchestration layer vs becoming your own BSP
page.h1: Using an orchestration layer vs becoming your own BSP
page.metaTitle: Orchestration layer vs becoming your own BSP
page.metaDescription: Why the platform sits above the provider APIs rather than holding carrier relationships: your rates, registrations and sender identity stay yours.
page.lede: We chose to sit above the provider APIs rather than hold carrier relationships — because that is the arrangement that keeps your rates, your registrations and your sender identity in your own name. Here is what that choice puts in your hands.

sections.h: What we do, and what that keeps yours
bullets: We add routing, failover and pacing on the SMS channel, plus normalized receipts, suppression and a send log above the accounts you already hold
Carrier relationships and registrations stay with your provider, filed in your name
Nothing in the middle can reprice your traffic or lift a carrier filter
Your volume commitments and your sender identities are never held by us

sections.h: What holding carrier relationships actually requires
p: Holding carrier relationships is a permanent engineering and regulatory commitment — registrations, sender verification, country rules, and commercial liability for delivery. Those obligations exist in both models; becoming a BSP adds the sending platform on top of them rather than replacing them.
bullets: Standing up senders is the easy part of either route
The hard part is the permanent obligations, which do not disappear when you self-host
Receipt normalization is ongoing work, because each provider reports in its own vocabulary and changes it

sections.h: Built for teams whose product is something else
p: The layer is built for teams whose product is something else: it keeps messaging dependable without letting it become the business. If messaging is itself what you sell, owning the carrier relationship may well be the point, and the layer still sits above it — the two arrangements are not exclusive, and choosing this one does not stop you from holding relationships of your own.

faq.q: Does Whaleal hold a carrier relationship?
faq.a: No, and that is deliberate. Staying above your provider is what keeps your rates, your registrations and your sender identity in your own name rather than in ours.

faq.q: Will the platform file registrations for me?
faq.a: Registration and sender verification are filed by you, in your own name — which is exactly why they stay with you whichever way you send.

It depends what you count. What the layer takes off your plate is the permanent part: the engineering attention a sending platform needs after the first message works — pacing, failover, receipt normalization and suppression as providers change.
